reference: The system util-linux renice(1) CLI, invoked by the same fixture under system Bash. Runnable parity inputs are missing or malformed and must be rejected before setpriority; reference status and output are collected independently. Metadata expectations come from Bash type/help behavior and the documented renice_doc contract in /source/loadables/renice.c and /source/docs/sol-renice.md. No candidate output is used to construct an expectation.
coverage: Bash reports renice as a builtin and exposes its documented short help description.
GNU CLI parity for missing operands, malformed priority, malformed PID, and unresolved username; these inputs are rejected before any priority mutation.
Deferred owned-child checks for absolute priority semantics, selector and username resolution, priority boundaries and kernel errors, and continuation after per-target failures.
exclusions: No valid target is passed to renice in a runnable case, and no priority-changing operation is executed.

Process, process-group, and all-user mutations; target-zero semantics; kernel clamping and permission behavior; and syscall continuation require a disposable child or independently reviewed setpriority/passwd mock and are recorded as deferred.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash exposes the selected loadable as a builtin, using the type builtin without invoking renice.
Check the short help summary against the first documented renice_doc line; help is metadata and does not change process state.
cases.stdout: renice - Set absolute niceness of running processes.

cases.purpose: Compare the CLI's missing-operand rejection. No priority or target is supplied, so no target can be changed.
Verify a non-decimal priority is rejected before the numeric target is considered; GNU renice is the independent status/output oracle.
Compare rejection of a nonnumeric PID. The operand cannot name a process, so this exercises validation without a setpriority target.
Compare rejection of a username absent from the fixture's isolated passwd database; lookup failure occurs before any all-user operation.
Check -n as an absolute priority, including POSIXLY_CORRECT behavior, on a short-lived owned child; independently query the child's final priority and confirm the shell parent is unchanged.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with an owned child and independent getpriority verification. Run the same operation through GNU util-linux renice and the candidate, with POSIXLY_CORRECT=1, and never target the invoking shell or an unrelated PID.

cases.purpose: Verify -p, -g, and -u selection, selector transitions, selectors before the priority, numeric and named users, and zero-ID interpretation.
cases.reason: Requires an independently reviewed setpriority interception plus deterministic passwd lookup fixture. Record each (which, id, priority) request and prove the mock never forwards calls to the kernel; all-user selection must remain mock-only.

cases.purpose: Check signed-int boundary parsing, Linux upper-priority clamping, and denial of negative priority without changing the parent.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with one owned child, RLIMIT_NICE=0, no effective CAP_SYS_NICE, and independent getpriority checks before and after each call. The child must be the only target and must exit during fixture cleanup.

cases.purpose: Verify that invalid targets and injected ESRCH/EPERM failures set a failing status while later targets are still attempted, and that usage errors make no calls.
cases.reason: Requires a reviewed setpriority mock that returns deterministic per-target errors and records all requests without forwarding them. Compare request order, final status, and silent-success output against GNU renice; do not use real process targets.
